**SEC. 123. Virginia Class Submarine Multiyear Procurement**
- Purpose: Authorize multiyear contracts for up to 13 Virginia class submarines (block VI configured).
- Subject to 10 USC 3501.
- Advance procurement authority beginning FY2024 for long lead time material or economic order quantities.
- Out-year payments (post-FY2025) subject to availability of appropriations.
- Termination liability capped at amount appropriated for covered submarines.

**SEC. 124. Auxiliary Personnel Lighter Program**
- Contract authority beginning FY2024 for up to 6 APL class vessels and associated material.
- Payments subject to availability of appropriations; termination liability limited to total funding obligated at time of termination.

**SEC. 125. V-22 Nacelle Improvement Program Limitation**
- Secretary of Defense must upgrade not fewer than 24 V-22 aircraft per FY2024 President's budget plan.
- Exception: Secretary may reduce below 24 with certification to congressional defense committees that reduction is in national security interest.

**SEC. 126. Government-Operated Dry Docks in San Diego Solicitations**
- Navy solicitations for private sector non-nuclear surface ship maintenance in San Diego may include Government-operated dry docks only if insufficient private capacity exists.
- Per 10 USC 2466.
- Applies to solicitations issued after enactment; terminates 5 years after enactment.

**SEC. 127. Annual Reports on Government Docks for Ship Repair**
- Secretary of Navy reports to congressional defense committees by June 30, 2024, annually through 2028.
- Identifies instances where Navy used Government dock when private capacity was available; explains reasons.

**SEC. 131. F-15 Aircraft Retirement Limitation**
- Amends 10 USC 9062 by adding subsection (l): During enactment date through September 30, 2029, Secretary of Air Force may not retire more than 68 F-15E aircraft, reduce funding presuming future divestment, or keep F-15E in "XJ" status.
- Exception: individual aircraft determined case-by-case no longer mission capable/uneconomical to repair.
- Amends Section 150 of FY2023 NDAA (PL 117-263): adds reporting requirements for each F-15E to be divested (upgrades, modifications, dates, costs, remaining service-life).
- Annual updates due October 1, 2024, and each year through 2029.
- Retirement authority under (l)(1)(A) does not apply until Secretary complies with Section 150 requirements as amended.

**SEC. 132. RQ-4 Aircraft Limitations**
- Amends 10 USC 9062 by adding subsection (m): During enactment date through September 30, 2028, Secretary may not retire RQ-4 aircraft, reduce funding presuming divestment, keep in XJ status, or decrease total inventory below 10.
- Same case-by-case exception for non-mission-capable aircraft.

**SEC. 133. Temporary Exception to Fighter Aircraft Minimum Inventory**
- Notwithstanding 10 USC 9062(i)(1), during covered period (enactment through October 1, 2024), Secretary may decrease fighter PMAI to not fewer than 1,112 aircraft.
- After covered period, original minimum requirements apply.

**SEC. 523. Prohibition on Former Members Accepting Post-Service Employment with Certain Foreign Governments**
- Adds new 10 U.S.C. §989 to chapter 49, title 10.
- **Prohibition (sub. (a)):** Covered individuals may not occupy covered post-service positions.
- **Waiver (sub. (b)):** SecDef may grant temporary waiver (max 5 years, renewable) if national security interests advanced. Revocable if threat to national security. Written application required. Within 30 days of issuance/revocation, notify SASC/HASC with specified elements.
- **Certification (sub. (c)):** Before retirement/separation, each member informed in writing of prohibition and penalties; must certify understanding.
- **Penalties (sub. (d)):** For knowing/willful violations: withhold pay/allowances/benefits; revoke security clearance.

Includes number of former covered individuals in covered positions (by employer, foreign government, nature of services); assessment of compliance systems, threats, federal law violations. Unclassified, may include classified annex.
- **Threat notifications (sub. (f)):** Within 30 days of determining threat or federal law violation, notify congressional defense committees with individual name, employer, foreign government, risk description.

- **Purpose/Mechanism:** Amends the Central Intelligence Agency Act of 1949 (50 U.S.C. 3501 et seq.) by adding Sections 30, 31, and 32 to establish comprehensive policies, reporting mechanisms (restricted and unrestricted), and an investigative body for sexual assault and sexual harassment allegations within the CIA.

- **Section 30 (50 U.S.C. 3531) - Director Responsibilities:**
  - Establish uniform training for employees handling allegations.
  - Develop policies to protect confidentiality and mitigate negative career/reputation effects for reporters.
  - Develop standards for mitigation/protection during investigations, employee consequences for substantiated allegations, career path protection, and mission protection.
  - Articulate/enforce norms for healthy workplace culture.
  - Issue workforce messaging globally.
  - Implement training (onboarding, annual refresher, specialized leadership) defining assault/harassment.
  - Implement training environment processes (in-person training within first 5 days of extended/residential courses).
  - Consult with FBI Victim Advocacy Specialists for training requirements.
  - Procedures for current/former employees to obtain records related to their reports.
